\section[hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum]{hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum — today's}

\label{lesson:LA-C215-hodiernus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for rare, thin, then the Latin for frequent, crowded.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum}
\textbf{hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum} — \textquotedblleft{}today's\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{hodiernus} is built on \emph{hodiē}, \textquotedblleft{}today\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with \emph{-ernus}, an ending for time: of today.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for rare, thin, then the Latin for frequent, crowded, then say \emph{hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does hodiernus, hodierna, hodiernum mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Today's\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[hesternus, hesterna, hesternum]{hesternus, hesterna, hesternum — yesterday's}

\label{lesson:LA-C215-hesternus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for frequent, crowded, then the Latin for today's.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: hesternus, hesterna, hesternum}
\textbf{hesternus, hesterna, hesternum} — \textquotedblleft{}yesterday's\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{hesternus} is built on the old stem \emph{hes-}, \textquotedblleft{}yesterday\textquotedblright{}, the stem behind \emph{herī}, \textquotedblleft{}yesterday\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with \emph{-ternus}, an ending for time.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hesternus, hesterna, hesternum}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hesternus, hesterna, hesternum}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{hesternus, hesterna, hesternum}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for frequent, crowded, then the Latin for today's, then say \emph{hesternus, hesterna, hesternum} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does hesternus, hesterna, hesternum mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Yesterday's\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum]{crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum — tomorrow's}

\label{lesson:LA-C215-crastinus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for today's, then the Latin for yesterday's.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum}
\textbf{crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum} — \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow's\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{crāstinus} is built on \emph{crās}, \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), with \emph{-tinus}, an ending for time. Where \emph{crās} comes from is uncertain.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for today's, then the Latin for yesterday's, then say \emph{crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does crāstinus, crāstina, crāstinum mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Tomorrow's\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[vērus, vēra, vērum]{vērus, vēra, vērum — true, real}

\label{lesson:LA-C215-verus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for yesterday's, then the Latin for tomorrow's.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: vērus, vēra, vērum}
\textbf{vērus, vēra, vērum} — \textquotedblleft{}true, real\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{vērus} is inherited, usually traced to Proto-Indo-European \emph{*weh1ros}, \textquotedblleft{}true\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1); German \emph{wahr}, \textquotedblleft{}true\textquotedblright{}, is a cousin. Lewis \& Short still called it doubtful.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vērus, vēra, vērum}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vērus, vēra, vērum}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{vērus, vēra, vērum}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for yesterday's, then the Latin for tomorrow's, then say \emph{vērus, vēra, vērum} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does vērus, vēra, vērum mean? (\textquotedblleft{}True, real\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[incertus, incerta, incertum]{incertus, incerta, incertum — uncertain}

\label{lesson:LA-C215-incertus}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Latin for tomorrow's, then the Latin for true.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: incertus, incerta, incertum}
\textbf{incertus, incerta, incertum} — \textquotedblleft{}uncertain\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{incertus} is \emph{in-}, \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}, with \emph{certus}, \textquotedblleft{}sure\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{incertus, incerta, incertum}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{incertus, incerta, incertum}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{incertus, incerta, incertum}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Latin for tomorrow's, then the Latin for true, then say \emph{incertus, incerta, incertum} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does incertus, incerta, incertum mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Uncertain\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
